evidence:
The arithmetic and authored separation of credit are supported, but the required empirical discrimination evidence is missing. I inspected the actual frozen XLSX using openpyxl: Quality Checks!row 41 (check 40) says, "The rubric produces a spread across partial-quality apps, not all-or-nothing"; Internal Quality Checks!row 41 repeats it. The frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:165-166 requires a spread and warns against a single precondition collapsing all signal. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Runtime and model evidence, requires current-hash runtime evidence for reward discrimination; qc/README.md:25-27 explicitly lists this check and says runtime gaps block clearance.

Source result: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/scoring.toml has positive 0.6 Functional / 0.2 Polish / 0.2 Visual weights, two 0.0 gates, and the canonical functional floor 0.05. All three scored judge.toml files use weighted_mean. Parsing every criterion yields 58 binary Functional rows with total weight 32.7, seven binary Polish rows with total weight 4.0, and six five-point Likert Visual rows with total weight 6.0. Visual has all five described anchors and its prompt.md:39-42 specifies (raw - 1) / 4 normalization. The exact score.py and scoring.toml bytes equal the frozen template copies. score.py (main, weighted/floors/reward calculation) computes the weighted score and returns rounded partial reward only when both gates and the strict functional > 0.05 floor pass. This is intentionally shaped scoring, not a binary final reward; the canonical floor itself is not a defect.

Bounded execution: I invoked the actual frozen score.py main through Python 3.12 runpy.run_path on temporary gates/reward.json and scored/reward.json inputs (no RewardKit, browser, Docker, provider, or app run). With both gates = 1 and Polish = Visual = 0.5, Functional inputs 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 produced actual reward outputs 0.3500, 0.5000 and 0.6500. All dimensions = 1 produced 1.0000. Either failed gate produced 0.0000 and scorer exit 1, even when supplied scored inputs were all 1. Functional = 0.05 with Polish = Visual = 1 produced reward 0.0000 (weighted_score 0.4300); Functional = 0.05001 produced 0.4300. These are synthetic aggregate-input scorer measurements, not measured scores for apps. A weight-subset calculation found 621 distinct above-floor Functional sums; that is only arithmetic capacity, not evidence that all corresponding products exist.

Independent-credit inspection: Functional prompt.md:9 says "Never ... inherit another row's verdict, or apply an all-legs score to a whole protocol"; :11 and :101-113 require continued unrelated observations and independent setup. Examples are the lowercase/JS CSS controls at :143-149, harmless-word fallback at :220, error-message/line collection despite rollback setup failure at :253, and fresh-record post-restart write fallback at :367-369. Functional judge.toml separates stale server refusal (weight 1.8) from dirty-editor recovery (weight 2.0), and restart durability (2.0) from post-restart writing (0.5). Polish prompt.md:34-39 and :49 preserves separate observations. Visual prompt.md:13-22 does not automatically turn an execution defect into a visual defect. No source-level all-or-nothing collapse was demonstrated for otherwise gate-passing apps.

Adversarial readings: A conforming frontend serving library records in a server-rendered document, using native/composite controls and proactively preventing a stale Save is expressly accepted by the constraints gate, Functional prompt.md:5, app_context.md:13, and Polish prompt.md:43-49; those choices do not require a zero or inherited failure. A broken app that correctly refuses stale requests but discards the dirty editor must fail only the relevant recovery outcome while retaining supported server-refusal credit. Injecting that isolated 2.0/32.7 loss, with all other aggregate credit retained, produced 0.9633 rather than 0 or 1; this is a conditional arithmetic witness, not an executed app mutant. A static hardcoded shell cannot meet the render gate's authored marker proof, and client-only storage cannot meet the constraints gate's clean-context server readback. Their failed-gate vectors were actually zeroed by score.py. No actual false-pass or false-fail implementation was established for this row.

Available runtime evidence: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json names case=golden, paid_provider=false, browser_driver="direct pinned Playwright", oracle_score_claimed=false, and wall_seconds=98.02680282300571. Its pre and post scope is "Continuous local reference browser proof; no LLM/provider/platform execution" and criterion_verdicts_produced=false. I verified its Functional judge and prompt SHA256 values against the frozen bytes. I also inspected actual S22 and S23 readback/refusal/dirty-retention observations: they establish successful golden behaviors, not differences among partial-quality app rewards. The executed launch_workflow.py combines product fact booleans into passed; it does not run the configured judge/scorer. The current run directory has no runtime-evidence.json, reward.json, reward.txt or rewardkit.log. The configured judge remains task.toml:31-32 claude-code / z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, invoked by tests/test.sh's two RewardKit suites. No current-hash configured-judge results for partial apps were available. Therefore this check is not upgraded to Pass: source design and actual arithmetic are supported, empirical app-score discrimination remains unmeasured.
suggested_fix: When authorized, run the unchanged full configured judge on a bounded set of real partial app variants that preserve both baseline gates, including separate stale-refusal/draft-loss and restart-durability/write variants, plus a weak gate-failing control. Preserve raw criterion outputs, rewards, commands and hashes in a current-input runtime-evidence.json record. Do not substitute synthetic scorer inputs or golden Playwright timing for those measurements.
